newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Air Lines returns to skies on smaller scale.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Air Lines returns to skies on smaller scale.

text.p: Kiwi Air Lines, which suspended flights in October after seeking bankruptcy protection, said it returned to scheduled service Monday after it obtained an additional $3.5 million in financing.
The Newark, N.J.-based carrier filed for bankruptcy in September under a heavy debt load, and suspended flights on Oct. 15 as part of its Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization.
On Jan. 15, Kiwi received U.S. Bankruptcy Court approval for a $3.5 million letter of credit facility from Edwards-Wasatch Enterprises, an investment group based in Boynton Beach, Fla.

Edwards-Wasatch, which is now the controlling stockholder of Kiwi, previously approved $5 million debtor-in-possession financing to Kiwi. It has committed to raise additional funds upon reorganization of Kiwi, the airline said.
A Kiwi spokesman said the airline planned to file its reorganization plan in the next few months.
Kiwi relaunched service between Newark, N.J.; Chicago; Atlanta and West Palm Beach, Fla., with a fleet of seven 727-200 aircraft and 500 employees.
At its peak, Kiwi had 15 aircraft and 1,200 employees.
Initially, Kiwi said it will offer unrestricted fares of $79 and $99 until Jan. 31. Until Feb. 12, passengers will receive "Buy Once. Fly Twice." coupons good for a flight later in 1997.
